newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends sharply higher on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends sharply higher on fund buying.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended sharply higher on heavy fund buying while soyoil futures closed firm on spillover strength from a rally in soybeans, traders said.
"Stops were hit in beans, oats and meal late and funds bought about 6,000 (lots) meal on the day," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.

Buyers keyed off of Wednesday's USDA supply and demand report which showed a 15-million-bushel cut in U.S. ending soybean stocks. USDA left soymeal ending stocks unchanged but raised export usage by 150,000 tons to 6.65 million tons.
That increase was offset by a jump in production to 33.34 million tons from 33.19 million in January's report.

USDA also trimmed U.S. soyoil ending stocks by 50 million lbs to 1.965 billion lbs. That reflected a sharp increase in export demand to 1.850 billion lbs, above the previous estimate of 1.750 billion.
Soymeal ended $5.60 to $1.80 per ton higher with March up $5.10 at $247.20. Soyoil closed 0.35 to 0.05 cent per lb higher with March up 0.05 at 23.98.
Funds were active buyers of soymeal. Smith Barney reportedly bought 1,000 lots December.
Griffin Trading bought 500 lots May, Refco Inc bought 600 March and Merrill Lynch, R.J. O'Brien and Tenco Inc each bought 400 lots, traders said.
Cargill Inc sold 800 lots March and bought 300 March while ADM sold 500 March.
In soyoil, ADM sold 800 lots May, Term Commodities bought 800 lots March and Produce Grain bought 600 May.
LIT America bought 500 May while Rosenthal Collins sold 1,000 March and Prudential Securities sold 600 March and 400 July, traders said.

Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 22,000 lots, against Tuesday's actual volume of 16,248 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 15,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's volume of 9,158 lots, CBOT reported.
